commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Tightens Hawaii tax-table and MFS holds: scope tightening of an existing module.
description: This PR therefore holds **all nonitemizer public tax/liability stages** rather than assuming $20,000 is the ceiling or substituting continuous §235-51 schedules.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix hold conditioned on `hi_pit_2026_taxable_income <= hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling` with that parameter pinned at 20000, i.e. it treated HRS 235-53(a)(2)'s statutory floor ("the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director") as the Director's actual ceiling, so nonitemizers with taxable income above $20,000 were published a continuous 235-51 schedule tax that the source may instead route to the unpinned Director-prescribed table.
triage.triage_notes: Read HRS 235-53, 235-55.6, 235-55.7 and 235-55.85 through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py succeeded for all four). 235-53(a)(1)-(2) confirms the ceiling is a Director-determined amount with only a $20,000 floor, so the pre-fix ceiling value and the branch it gated had no source basis; the fix deletes the conjunct (hold now = `not hi_pit_2026_elects_itemized_deductions`) and re-gates the four public tax/liability stages on `not hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies`. Companion-test deltas corroborate the behavior change: supported_profile_tax_before_credits goes 2024.632 -> 0 (and 3401.264 -> 0, 13046.056 -> 0) with tax_table_source_hold_applies flipping not_holds -> holds, and the 2024.632 value survives only in the new private hi_pit_2026_profile_candidate_* rules. MULTI-DEFECT COMMIT: the same module diff also fixes at least three further fidelity gaps, each an unrepresented_clause if scored separately - (a) hi_pit_2026_refundable_child_and_dependent_care_credit had no marital restriction at all, and the fix adds `(not MFS or mfs_is_legally_separated or mfs_living_apart_conditions_met)` matching 235-55.6(e)(2) "the credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return" with the (e)(3)/(e)(4) exceptions; (b) hi_pit_2026_food_credit_qualified_exemption_count omitted 235-55.85(c) "a minor child receiving support from the department of human services of the State, social security survivor's benefits, and the like, may be considered a dependent and a qualified exemption", and the fix adds the DHS and SSA-survivor counts plus a hold on the open-ended "and the like" category; (c) the food/excise and renter credits ignored the 235-55.85(b) and 235-55.7(e) provisos that separate filers "shall claim only the tax credit to which they would have been entitled had a joint return been filed", and the fix fails closed for MFS rather than encoding the counterfactual. I chose the tax-table item as the decisive path because it is first in the commit subject, drives the largest behavioral change, and is the one the PR body explains verbatim; a reviewer preferring the clause-level view could reclassify the kind as unrepresented_clause (or amount_mismatch for the $20,000 ceiling parameter, which the fix leaves in the file at 20000 but no longer uses in the hold). Direction caveat: because the tax-table hold left supported_profile_applies, this commit also NEWLY publishes supported_profile_taxable_income and supported_profile_refundable_credits for nonitemizers (test deltas 0 -> 9000, 0 -> 570, 0 -> 100); that widening is added grounded coverage, not a defect fix. Domain-bound additions to hi_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid (failure counts bounded by exemption counts, incapable_spouse_count <= 1) are fail-closed hardening rather than a source disagreement. Commit message body is empty; PR #1035 has no reviews or review comments, so the PR body is the only narrative evidence, and it describes the PR's end state rather than this commit alone - hence confidence below 0.8.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix hold rule conditioned on `hi_pit_2026_taxable_income <= hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling` with that parameter pinned at '20000', and because `supported_profile_applies` required `not tax_table_source_hold_applies`, nonitemizers with taxable income above $20,000 were published a continuous §235-51 amount at the public tax, tax-after-nonrefundable-credit, and signed-net stages. HRS 235-53(a)(2) read through the pinned release defines the ceiling as "the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director for the tax rate category in which such taxpayer falls", so $20,000 is a floor on an unknown, category-specific ceiling, and (a)(1) imposes the Director's table "[i]n lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51" up to that ceiling — the encoded threshold therefore had no basis in the cited source. The fix deletes the comparison outright and re-attaches the hold to the four public tax/liability stages, which is the removal of an ungrounded branch condition rather than a correction of a number or of a comparison's side. amount_mismatch fails because no corrected value replaces 20000, and boundary_direction fails because no strictness or floor/ceiling flip could ground a bound the corpus does not contain.
triage.verifier_notes: Verified against the pinned provision (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, us-hi/statute/235-53, body sha256 af53064f5b577b40c8fe75855a968f2913a1095d38403da1865d496982b92317): "(2) Ceiling amount defined. ... the term \"ceiling amount\" means, with respect to any taxpayer, the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director for the tax rate category in which such taxpayer falls." Pre-state (a8ca13ee) lines 837-854 pin the parameter to '20000'; lines 1217-1238 hold rule; line 999 places the hold inside supported_profile_applies. Post-state (26ebd1a18c) lines 2139/2184/2207/2231 add `and not hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies` to tax_before_credits, tax_after_nonrefundable_credits, net_income_tax_liability, refundable_excess_before_payments, while supported_profile_taxable_income (2099) and supported_profile_refundable_credits (2144) stay published — the hold is targeted at table-dependent stages, not blanket. Residual issues for a reviewer: (1) the parameter hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling ('20000') survives at post line 836 but is referenced by no formula (dead parameter); (2) moving the hold out of supported_profile_applies also newly publishes refundable credits for nonitemizers with taxable income <= $20,000, which is added coverage, not the defect; (3) the commit bundles other, separate fidelity changes outside this rule_path (MFS bar on food/renter credits, §235-55.6 living-apart exception for CDCC, §235-55.85 DHS/SSA-survivor minor-child counts, new input-domain bounds) that would classify as unrepresented_clause / wrong_entity_or_scope if scored on their own; (4) this is a review repair round inside PR #1035, the PR that introduced the module, so the defective state never landed on main. The first reader's PR-body quote ("rather than assuming $20,000 is the ceiling or substituting continuous §235-51 schedules") describes exactly the pre-state this commit removed, so the quote corroborates rather than merely restates.
